sentences.text: Counsel for the petitioner is directed to add National Highway Authority of India as a respondent in course of the day.
Patna High Court CWJC No.4379 of 2023(2) dt.08-08-2023 3.
Office is directed to add the National Highways Authority of India as the respondent no.10 in the cause title page.

4. Counsel for the petitioner submits that the present writ petition has been filed for directing the respondent to pay the half of the amount of compensation to the petitioner, which awarded in lieu of land acquisition bearing Khata No.456, Khesara No.557 and an area of 0.0845 Hect. (Approximately 21 Decimal) situated at Circle Officer-Jandaha, Vaishali.
Counsel submits that the said land has been acquired for the purpose of construction of National Highway No.103 (New 322).
He submits that the said land is the subject matter of Land Acquisition Case No.17 of 2021-22 and the said notice has come in the name of petitioner and his brother namely Vimal Kishor Mehrotra.
Counsel further submits that petitioner is entitled for the claimed amount.
5. Counsel for the private respondent submits that petitioner has already sold his property and now demanding compensation, which is not right.
Counsel also submits that a separate Jamabandi running in the name of both the brothers i.e. petitioner and his brother namely Vimal Kishor Mehrotra bearing Title Partition Suit No.839 of 2022.

Patna High Court CWJC No.4379 of 2023(2)
dt.08-08-2023 6.
Counsel for National Highways Authority of India submits that notices have been issued in the name of both said the brothers i.e. petitioner and his brother namely Vimal Kishor Mehrotra.

He further submits that under Section 3H of the National Highway Act, 1956 [Act No. 48 of 1956] the power has been conferred to the competent authority (District Land Acquisition Officer) to decide on such matters.

7. In this background, the petitioner is directed to file a representation within four weeks from the date of this order before the competent authority under Section 3H of the National Highway Act,
1956 [Act No. 48 of 1956] and upon receiving the representation, the competent authority, after hearing all the concerned parties, shall decide on this matter and pass a reasoned and speaking order within 6 weeks after receiving the representation in accordance with law under Section 3H of the National Highway Act, 1956 [Act No. 48 of 1956].
8. With the aforesaid direction, this writ petition is hereby disposed off.

(Dr. Anshuman, J.) Ashishsingh/-
